L137: IMDM (Iscove's Modified Dulbecco's Medium) is well suited for rapidly proliferating, high-density cell cultures, including Jurkat, COS-7, and macrophage cells. L147: Using IMDM
L148: IMDM, a modification of Dulbecco's Modified Eagle Medium, includes selenium as well as additional amino acids and vitamins. In addition, this unique medium lacks iron, with potassium nitrate replacing ferric nitrate. IMDM with 【61†GlutaMAX™†www.invitrogen.com】 supplement minimizes toxic ammonia build-up and improves cell viability and growth in an easy-to-use format. IMDM contains no proteins, lipids, or growth factors.
L149: Therefore, IMDM requires supplementation, commonly with 10% 【62†Fetal Bovine Serum†www.invitrogen.com】 (FBS). IMDM uses a sodium bicarbonate buffer system (3.024 g/L), and therefore requires a 5–10% CO_{2} environment to maintain physiological pH.

L188: ## Frequently asked questions (FAQs)
L189: 
L190: ### How long can I keep my media after supplementing with serum?
L191: 
L192: Generally speaking, media can be used for up to three weeks after supplementation with serum. There are no formal studies to support this, but it is the rule of thumb used by our scientists.
L193: Find additional tips, troubleshooting help, and resources within our 【63†Mammalian Cell Culture Basics Support Center】.
L194: ### My medium was shipped at room temperature but it is supposed to be stored refrigerated. Is it okay?
L195: 
L196: We routinely ship media that require long-term storage in the refrigerator at room temperature. We have done studies on representative media formulations to show that media can be at room temperature for up to a week without a problem.
L197: Find additional tips, troubleshooting help, and resources within our 【63†Mammalian Cell Culture Basics Support Center】.
L198: ### Will depletion, absence, or breakdown of essential growth-promoting components such as glutamine or growth factors reduce the growth rate of my culture?
L199: Yes. If you suspect that this is the case, remove the medium and add fresh medium. Alternatively, you can supplement medium with growth-promoting components. It is also possible to substitute GlutaMax I or II for glutamine in the medium to prevent glutamine exhaustion.
L200: Find additional tips, troubleshooting help, and resources within our 【64†Cell Culture Support Center】.
L201: ### Will the media formulations containing GlutaMAX supplement change with respect to L-glutamine content?
L202: 
L203: In all media containing GlutaMAX supplement dipeptides as a substitute for L-glutamine, concentration is equimolar with the L-glutamine in the original formulation.
L204: Find additional tips, troubleshooting help, and resources within our 【64†Cell Culture Support Center】.
L205: ### How can I remove mycoplasma contamination from my cell culture medium?
L206: Very often mycoplasma contamination cannot be removed from the culture so it should be discarded. You may have a unique culture that you prefer not to discard and would like to try to clean it. Ciprofloxacin and Plasmocin have reportedly been used for this application. If interested in a protocol or directions for use, check with the antibiotic supplier or published literature.
L207: Note that mycoplasma are very difficult to remove from culture and spread easily so the treated cultures should be quarantined until clear of mycoplasma, and your laboratory should be thoroughly cleaned.
L208: Find additional tips, troubleshooting help, and resources within our 【64†Cell Culture Support Center】.
